hints: Look closely at the two functional groups in H2C=C(CH3)CH2CO2CH3, an alkene at one end and a methyl ester at the other.
Hydrolysis of the CO2CH3 group can only give methanol plus a carboxylic acid, and there is no CH3CO or CH3CH(OH) group for the iodoform test.
Remember hot concentrated KMnO4 cleaves the C=C bond and hot aqueous acid also hydrolyses the ester, so track what happens to the C(CH3) end.
walkthrough:
**Identify the functional groups**

Great start, let's draw out what we have. The molecule is methyl 3-methylbut-3-enoate.

$$ \text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3 $$

On the left we have a terminal alkene, $\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)-$. On the right we have a methyl ester, $-\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$.

**Check hydrolysis and synthesis**

Acid or alkaline hydrolysis of a methyl ester always gives methanol, $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$, which is a primary alcohol, not a secondary alcohol.

$$ \text{RCO}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{RCOOH} + \text{CH}_3\text{OH} $$

For synthesis, the acid part comes from $\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{COOH}$, a C5 unsaturated acid, not ethanoic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$.

**Check iodoform and oxidative cleavage**

A positive iodoform test with alkaline $\text{I}_2(aq)$ needs $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$ or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}(\text{OH})-$. This molecule has $\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{CH}_2$ and $\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$, neither of which reacts.

With hot concentrated acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$, the $\text{C}=\text{C}$ is cleaved. $\text{H}_2\text{C}=$ is oxidised fully to $\text{CO}_2$, while $=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)-$ becomes $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}-$:
$$ \text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3 $$

Under the hot aqueous acidic conditions the methyl ester then hydrolyses to $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{COOH}$ plus $\text{CH}_3\text{OH}$. This matches the stated product.

options.A: False. Hydrolysis of the methyl ester group gives the carboxylic acid H2C=C(CH3)CH2COOH and methanol, CH3OH. Methanol is a primary alcohol, so a secondary alcohol cannot be formed.
options.B: False. Esterification keeps the acid carbon skeleton. Here the acyl part is H2C=C(CH3)CH2CO-, from 3-methylbut-3-enoic acid, not from ethanoic acid, CH3COOH. Methanol provides the CH3O part.
options.C: False. The iodoform test is positive only for methyl ketones, CH3CO-, and secondary alcohols of type CH3CH(OH)-. The CH3 groups here are in (CH3)C=C and CO2CH3, so no yellow CHI3 precipitate forms.
options.D: Correct. Hot concentrated acidified KMnO4 oxidatively cleaves the terminal alkene: H2C= gives CO2 and =C(CH3)CH2CO2CH3 gives CH3COCH2CO2CH3. Hot aqueous acid then hydrolyses this keto-ester to CH3COCH2COOH and CH3OH.
